summary: The 9-8-8 Connect Act awards grants to crisis centers for follow-up check-ins and referrals after 988 calls or mobile crisis responses, and requires the FCC to ensure all mobile carriers transmit 988 calls and texts (including from non-service phones) while mandating direct 988 dialing on multi-line phone systems.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly authorizes $30,000,000 in appropriations for FY 2027 to fund grants to crisis centers for follow-up suicide prevention services. This constitutes new federal spending, directly expanding government outlays in the public health domain.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue collection.

Section 2 amends the Public Health Service Act to create a grant program for follow-up mental health crisis services, expanding publicly funded suicide prevention and behavioral health intervention infrastructure.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration policy, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions concern military or defense spending or policy.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The grant program expands publicly funded mental health crisis follow-up services, which function as an extension of the social safety net for individuals in behavioral health emergencies.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance use policy.
No provisions address policing, sentencing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By authorizing new appropriations without offsetting revenue, the bill implicitly accepts additional deficit spending rather than prioritizing debt reduction.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.

Section 3 directs the FCC to promulgate regulations requiring commercial mobile service providers to transmit all 9-8-8 calls and texts (including from non-service-initialized handsets) and amends rules for multi-line telephone systems, imposing new regulatory requirements on telecommunications providers.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil rights enforcement.
